intro: Broadcasting a channel vector across rows applies the same instrument calibration to each observation. The offset belongs after multiplication by the gain, which matters when the gain is negative.
task: Broadcast channel gains and offsets over readings, then clip each channel to its physical range.
requirements: readings has shape (samples, channels). The four vectors have one entry per channel; lower must be <= upper elementwise.
Return {"values": clipped calibrated matrix, "clipped": boolean matrix}. Calibration is readings*gains+offsets. A value exactly on a bound is not clipped.
Negative gains are allowed. Bounds apply after calibration, separately for each channel.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

examples.name: Two channels
examples.output:
{'values': [[3.0, -2.0], [8.0, 2.0]], 'clipped': [[False, True], [True, False]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 10 significant digits.)

examples.name: Bounds are inclusive
examples.output:
{'values': [[0.0, 1.0]], 'clipped': [[False, False]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 10 significant digits.)

examples.name: Negative gain
examples.output:
{'values': [[3.0], [0.0]], 'clipped': [[False], [True]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 10 significant digits.)

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Represent channel parameters as vectors matching the second matrix axis.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Compute calibrated values first, then compare with both bounds before clipping.

explanation: Broadcasting a channel vector across rows applies the same instrument calibration to each observation. The offset belongs after multiplication by the gain, which matters when the gain is negative.
The mask distinguishes changed measurements from values that happen to equal a limit. Keeping that mask supports auditing saturated sensors without confusing valid endpoint readings with clipping.
